dependency_text: The strict splits, merges and irreducible games of ENCODED-READERS and READER-SPLIT; the birth choices of LOCAL-COMMUTE.
objective: At the owner's go-ahead ("Let's do 1") on direction 1 of ENCODED-READERS-20261127-001: read each failing pair of a commuting choice as the cycle of its four cross pairs (pairs of knots holding one value each), prove that the closing sign is the parity of how often those cycles list their shared cross pairs in a reference order (so order-consistent choices close even), check it on every choice of the populations, and measure which of these structures growth's closures and the census types make. G18 Comparing growth laws. Stop when every frozen prediction is scored.
status: Complete 2026-11-27 (capability gained; a theorem by hand checked on 2,499,769 list appearances; refereed, R1 confirmed with fixes, no Block): the closing sign of every commuting choice is the parity of its failing pairs' cycles' listings of their cross pairs at every even coverage, so orientable and two-colourable choices close even; minimal strict odd choices covered twice are projective planes or Klein bottles after separation, through eight pairs (P1 held); on the tested grown closures a minimal strict choice is odd exactly when its cycles admit no balanced orders (6,534 even, all orientable), while the census types' non-orientable even choices all have more pairs than any grown one.
stop_rule: Stop when every frozen prediction is scored; no growth law is changed.
title: Cross pairs and the closing sign: is the readers' sign decided by the cycles its failing pairs make?
